instruction:
Execute `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rlc_bp.cir` in native PSpice. Use the native PSpice command-line simulator `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\psp_cmd.exe`. On this machine, use `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\Capture.exe` for OrCAD schematics and `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\allegro.exe` for board work.

Keep the native simulator artifacts as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rlc_bp.out`, `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rlc_bp_measure.txt`, and `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rlc_bp.dat`. Then read the sampled dB measurements from `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rlc_bp_measure.txt` and write `C:\Users\user\Desktop\metrics.json` with `f0`, `Q`, and `BW_3dB`. `f0` and `BW_3dB` are in Hz. `f0` is the peak sample frequency, and `BW_3dB` is the sampled-grid width between the lowest and highest frequencies that remain within 3 dB of the peak. Compute `Q` as `f0 / BW_3dB`.
